units.function: Large mocked startup integration suite covering decision-signing key generation/hardening, feedback service wiring, scheduler suppression, public-database refusal, detected-port auth origins and runtime API URL propagation.
units.dependencyDirection: Process environment and loaded deployment config enter the server composition root; mocked database/auth/services/server/filesystem dependencies expose startup decisions and returned runtime URLs.
units.keyDataModels: Deployment mode/exposure/bind/auth/database/storage/feedback config, decision-signing and JWT secrets, persisted key file/mode/symlink, scheduler suppression, service wiring, listen port, trusted origins and runtime API candidates.
units.lifecycle: Startup validates or generates signing material, repairs permissions/refuses a symlink, rejects unsafe authenticated-public database configurations, constructs services/app, starts selected maintenance loops and derives runtime/auth endpoints after port detection.
units.testAssessment: Strong security cases verify persisted signing-key directory/file modes, preservation of an existing key, symlink refusal and minimum explicit-secret length; public deployments fail before DB creation. Feedback coverage only proves the service object is passed to createApp, not that authorized pending rows flush correctly. The 725-line file mixes unrelated concerns and relies heavily on mocks, one captured interval callback and microtask timing; it lacks overlapping flush, graceful drain, retry/backoff, multi-instance coordination and no-egress-without-consent assertions.
units.designRationale: Exercise the real composition root without binding tests to live databases, sockets, auth providers or long-running schedulers, while preserving startup regressions accumulated across product areas.
units.companyOsProblem: Both deployment profiles need fail-closed startup security and explicit background-worker lifecycles, especially for irreversible data export and approval signing.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT signing-key no-follow/permission tests, preflight deployment refusal and detected-endpoint ordering. Split startup contracts by subsystem; make DataEgressWorker opt-in, lease/claim durable outbox rows atomically, prevent overlapping local runs, coordinate multiple replicas, use bounded backoff and await or checkpoint in-flight work during shutdown.
units.responsibilityConflict: Wiring a feedback service is not proof of authorized export. The app's immediate flush, 5-second interval and route-triggered flush can overlap because no in-flight guard is visible; rows are marked sent only after upload and the client lacks idempotency, so one consented trace can be transmitted more than once. Signing-key possession also proves server integrity, not human approval authority.
